searchText: Dunno how I feel about ephemeral code; generally almost all code is part of some application that is being used many times, so it's easier to just publish it once and then make a delegatecall wrapper of it I don't think this is always true. Imagine a user who wants to execute an AR itrary series of transactions that is unique to a particular use case (like Gnosis multisig transaction builder). While there will certainly be cases where two users do close enough to the same series of steps that you could generalize it into a single deployed instance of a thing (likely parameterized), the library of such things would be incredibly large and it is unknown up front which thing makes sense to generalize and which it doesn't. This means that from a practicality standpoint, reusing code in this context is non-trivial and likely not worth the engineering work to get right (not to mention it being more code that can go wrong).
